In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the formation of the Cooper pairs in the presence of strong random potential and Hubbard attraction is a non-universal process, and the Cooper pair size and the density of the Cooper pairs are strongly dependent on the random potential and the density of electrons in the system.

in the presence of strong random potential, in a low density ( n < 1) electron systems with strong onsite Hubbard interaction U > W, the formation of the inhomogeneous states with spatially separated Fermion and Bose components of the order parameter is possible.
the formation of boson droplets in the matrix of unpaired electrons in low density 2D electron systems is a generic feature of a wide range of electron densities and temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the framework of the model under study we observed the appearance of inhomogeneity of the superconductor state in the form of spatially separated droplets of Cooper pairs with different sizes and a decrease in their size at the same time with a decrease in the electron density.
the formation of droplets of the order parameter is possible only at low electron densities ( n ≪1), when the system has the possibility of phase separation.
the superconducting phase is stabilized by the random potential, and the normal phase is stabilized by a strong onsite attraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the presence of the strong onsite attraction and random potential the system can be considered as a mixture of Cooper pairs of different sizes and unpaired electrons.
the random potential plays an important role in the formation of the inhomogeneous state of spatially separated Cooper pairs and unbound electrons.
in a dirty metal the superconductivity is not destroyed by the disorder but rather is enhanced by it.
